_what_this_is: Retrieval corpus for the three paywall misses named in emc-fusion-partner-stratification.md §6 and in emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json -> retrieval_provenance.not_retrievable: Huang 2023 (PMID 36948401), Paioli 2021 (PMID 32572850), and the pazopanib phase 2 trial Stacchiotti 2019 (PMID 31331701, NCT02066285). Stacchiotti 2014 (PMID 24703573) is carried alongside because §4.4 rests on it too.
_method: Each source runs the same ladder rather than one guess at a URL: (1) OA-LOCATION DISCOVERY against four independent indexes (Unpaywall, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, OpenAIRE) plus the Europe PMC core record and fullTextUrlList, because 'paywalled in Europe PMC' and 'no legal free copy exists' are different claims and only the second closes a route; (2) a DIRECT publisher attempt at whatever location step 1 named; (3) a REGISTRY/secondary route (ClinicalTrials.gov v2, the EU Clinical Trials Register) for facts a trial report holds but a journal paywall does not cover; (4) the CITATION GRAPH, for a later series that reports the same stratification with counts.
_dispatch: python3 -c to strip the underscore keys, then .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml with targets_json=<that object>, targets_mode=replace, slug=<the round's slug>, ref=main. Dispatched at ref=main rather than the working branch because the corpus is INLINE, so nothing in the fetch depends on the branch's tree, and the working branch did not exist on origin.
_a_key_here_is_a_filename_not_a_result: A name in this file records what was ASKED FOR. Whether the fetch succeeded, and with what HTTP status, is in each round's _manifest.json on the literature-cache branch. Read the manifest, never this file, for what was actually retrieved.

_rounds.emc-partner-events: round 1 (run 31270016883, success) — OA discovery for all four papers + ClinicalTrials.gov v2 + Europe PMC citation lists.
_rounds.emc-partner-events-r2: round 2 (run 31270125124) — the bronze-OA publisher PDF that round 1's Unpaywall and OpenAlex records both named for Huang 2023, plus every institutional-repository handle OpenAlex/OpenAIRE listed for the three closed papers.
_rounds.emc-partner-events-r3: round 3 (run 31270164925, success) — the EU Clinical Trials Register entry for EudraCT 2013-005456-15 (= NCT02066285 = GEIS-32), whose number round 1's ClinicalTrials.gov record supplied.

_identifiers_returned_by_these_fetches._why_this_block_exists: These identifiers were RETURNED BY the fetches above (Europe PMC core records and OpenAlex work records), not typed from memory. They are recorded here so the prose that cites them in partner-event-counts-2026-08-08.md traces to a fetch product rather than to a model's recollection — the exact failure lint_citations.py was built for. Every DOI below was read out of the corresponding epmc_core_<pmid>.txt file on the literature-cache branch; none was guessed.
_identifiers_returned_by_these_fetches._a_guessed_doi_that_was_wrong_and_is_kep: round 4's key `unpaywall_37057757` was built from a DOI GUESSED as 10.1016/j.humpath.2023.04.002 on the assumption that PMID 37057757 sat in Human Pathology. It does not — it is Genes Chromosomes Cancer, DOI 10.1002/gcc.23144. The guessed DOI resolved to a real but completely unrelated paper about colonic sessile serrated lesions, and Unpaywall answered `is_oa: true` about THAT paper. A fabricated identifier that resolves is far more dangerous than one that 404s, because every downstream check succeeds. Caught by comparing the returned title against the expected one; the lesson is that an identifier must be read out of a record, never assembled from a journal guess.
